## Lie symmetries and detection

Each family is the orbit of a Lie symmetry. symident obtains the generators as the kernel of the
observability-identifiability matrix and proves scalings exactly
([Methods > Structural identifiability and Lie symmetries](methods-symmetries.html)).

## Detection settings

- `equilibrate = TRUE`: initial values are the steady state without TNFα.
- `reduceCQ = TRUE`: symmetries act on the conserved totals, the parameters of `Pimpl()`.
- `forcings = "TNF"`: TNFα is an input state, set by the event at time 0.
- `conditions`: a direction is non-identifiable only if it is so in both doses.

The imaging readouts bleach, $y = \log(s x + o) - \tau t$. In the control the states are constant,
so the bleaching rates are in no symmetry, and `symmetries.R` drops the bleaching terms.

## Symmetries of the full model

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/symmetries.rds", "symmetries.R"))
invisible(stored("results/reduction.rds", "symmetries.R"))
```

Computed by `symmetries.R`, loaded from `results/symmetries.rds`:

```{r symmetries, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
symmetries <- readRDS("results/symmetries.rds")
symmetries
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
types <- vapply(symmetries$symmetries, `[[`, "", "type")
```

The rank is `r symmetries$rank` of `r symmetries$dim` coordinates, proven; the kernel is spanned
by `r inWords(length(types))` scalings, each proven over the rationals. The generators are one
basis; up to sums there are four kinds.

- **Unobserved intermediates**, level against driven rate: receptor $X_1$, IκBα transcript $X_4$,
  A20 transcript $X_6$, A20 $X_7$ (with `inh_Ikk` and the A20 imaging scale).
- **Relative measurements**: IKK $X_2$; NFκB and IκBα together, printed as $X_3$ plus $X_4$ and
  $X_5$.
- **Nuclear volume** `Vnuc` against the rates reading nuclear concentrations, $X_5$.
- **A product**: `split_NfkIkb` appears only times `eta_split_pNfkpIkb`, $X_8$.

## Symmetry reduction

`symmetryReduction()` returns in `$trafo` a transformation without the directions, for scalings
by fixing one coordinate per direction
([Methods > Gauge and reduction](methods-symmetries.html#gauge-and-reduction)). Loaded from
`results/reduction.rds`:

```{r reduction, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
reduction <- readRDS("results/reduction.rds")
reduction
```

## Gauge fixing

`model.R` fixes one moved parameter per scaling at 1, 0 on log scale, the gauge:

```{r gauge}
```

The `r inWords(length(gauge))` coordinates remove all `r inWords(length(types))` scalings if their
weight matrix is regular
([Methods > Gauge and reduction](methods-symmetries.html#gauge-and-reduction)):

```{r}
W <- t(vapply(symmetries$symmetries, function(X)
  vapply(names(gauge), function(cn) as.numeric(X$weights[[cn]] %||% 0), 0), numeric(length(gauge))))
dimnames(W) <- list(paste0("X", seq_len(nrow(W))), names(gauge))
W
det(W)
```

This is the gauge of Oppelt et al. [@oppelt2018model]: concentrations are fractions of the NFκB
and IKK totals, receptor and transcripts are in units of the rates they drive, A20 in units of
the A20 imaging scale. [Optimization](guide-optimization.html) fits the remaining
`r length(setdiff(getParameters(p), names(gauge)))` parameters,
[Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html) checks which the data determine.

## Discrete symmetries

A discrete symmetry maps a parameter value to isolated other values with the same output.
`symmetryDetection(mode = "global")` counts these values and reconstructs rational maps between
them (requires msolve). `discrete.R` applies it to the reduced model of
[Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html#reduced-model), passed as `trafo`; loaded from
`results/discrete.rds`:

```{r discrete, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/discrete.rds", "discrete.R"))
```

```{r}
saved <- readRDS("results/discrete.rds")
discrete <- saved$discrete
discrete$info$discrete[c("count", "countFinal", "fundamentalDomain")]
swap <- discrete$discreteSymmetries[[1]]
swap[c("map", "level", "stateMaps")]
```

There are `r inWords(discrete$info$discrete$count)` values with the output of a generic one; the
map exchanges the degradation rates of the A20 transcript and of A20, `exact` means proven by the
map of the states. The map moves no coordinate of the scalings and holds in the original
coordinates as well.

The publication does not name the swap and reports both rates with the same 95 % interval,
$-5.97$ to $-3.32$ on log scale [@oppelt2018model, Table S7], the union of the two images.
`symmetryReduction(branch = )` gives a chart of the fundamental domain
`degrad_A20 < degrad_RnaA20`:

```{r fundamental, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
fundamental <- saved$fundamental
fundamental$trafo[c("degrad_A20", "degrad_RnaA20")]
```

`delta` is the positive difference of the two rates; in this chart a fit has one optimum instead
of two
([Profile likelihood > Profiles in the fundamental domain](guide-profiles.html#profiles-in-the-fundamental-domain)).

Reference: `symmetryDetection()`, `symmetryReduction()`, `discreteSymmetries()`
